2 غمّض الكَلَامَ , (S, K,) inf. n. تَغْمِيضٌ, (S,) He made the speech, or language, unapparent to the mind, not plain or perspicuous, obscure, recondite, or abstruse. (S, K, TA.) ―
-b2- غمّض حَدَّ السَّيْفِ, (A, TA,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) He made the edge of the sword thin [so that it might become hidden in the flesh when one smote with it]; (A, TA;) as also ↓ أَغْمَضَهُ . (K.) ＝
-A2- See also 4, in twelve places.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
